correctness.rationale: Every one of 65 explicit R-points satisfies the homogeneous sextic and all partial derivatives by direct Z[t]/(t²-t-1) arithmetic. For six types, Hessian determinant norms are 2^14, 2^34, 2^18, 2^38, 2^30, 2^30; for all 2080 point pairs the gcd of norms of six projective minors is a power of two. Because a vanishing modulo an odd prime forces divisibility of the integer norm by that prime, no collision or Hessian degeneration occurs in an odd-characteristic geometric fiber. Exact code was executed and an independent symbolic six-orbit cross-check succeeded. No assertion of total singular scheme exhaustion is made.

value.rationale: The number 65 is the classical extremal complex node count for a sextic. Determining precisely that the full classical node configuration has no odd bad prime is a natural arithmetic geometry question about stability of a highly singular integral model, especially at characteristic 3 and the ramified discriminant prime 5; generic openness would leave exceptional primes unidentified. The result provides an explicit split finite-etale subsystem of the relative singular locus over Z[t,1/2]/(t²-t-1) and a reusable exact descent certificate. The narrower claim is valuable without extrapolating to the full positive-characteristic singular scheme.
